result.title: RubricWorld: World Model-Guided Rubric Optimization for LLM Graders
result.comment: 25 pages including references and appendices; 6 figures, 8 tables
result.summary: Rubric optimization improves LLM grading by revising scoring instructions while keeping the grader's parameters fixed. Existing optimizers often judge edits by aggregate validation performance, limiting the supervision they retain about which errors an edit corrects or introduces. Testing each candidate also requires rescoring validation answers, which limits how many edits can be explored within a fixed budget. We propose RubricWorld, a framework that learns from previous edit evaluations to guide further search. Its world model predicts an edit's correction and degradation rates at score boundaries, conditioned on the current rubric state. The training signal comes from paired grading results: scores for the same answers before and after an edit. Predictions select one candidate for direct evaluation, and held-out confidence bounds determine whether it corrects enough target errors while keeping new errors within prespecified limits. Measured effects update the model even when the edit is rejected. Across EIR (National), ASAP2.0, and ASAP-SAS with three frozen LLM graders, RubricWorld achieves the highest score in 20 of 27 metric comparisons. On ASAP2.0, it raises gpt-5-mini accuracy from 18.20% with the original rubric to 46.70%, exceeding the strongest baseline, APO, by 22.60 percentage points. code will be released upon acceptance.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 RubricWorld：以世界模型在当前评分标准状态下预测一次编辑在分数边界上的纠错率与致错率，用同一批答案编辑前后的配对评分作训练信号，并按留出集置信界决定候选编辑是否采纳，从而在固定预算内减少反复重评。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「状态条件下预测动作效果＋配对前后监督＋预算内候选筛选与接受判据」的框架，可能为 latent 推理中的步级价值预测、贡献分配与停止决策提供可核查线索，但论文本身不含视觉或多模态推理内容。
